architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Blu.summary: Class Blueprint Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Represents a tray blueprint (a .blueprint file): a lot's objects and architecture (🔓) public sealed class Blueprint Inheritance object Blueprint Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The file is a 32-bit version and the length of its content, followed by the content compressed with Snappy (the raw block format). The content is a header, the LotObjects as a protobuf message, ObjectDefinitionMappings, Images and finally the Architecture as a record bundle. Blueprints without the header (HasHeader is false) hold only the objects and the architecture; Sims 4 Studio reads them, but none has been observed. Snappy compressors differ in their output, so Encode() reuses the compressed bytes it decoded when the content it would write is unchanged, and otherwise compresses the content anew. Decoding and encoding a blueprint the game wrote therefore reproduces it byte for byte. architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Flo.title: Class FloorIdGridSection | Llama Logic
architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Flo.summary: Class FloorIdGridSection Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Represents one of the seven floor id grids: the FloorKeysSection id painted on each quarter of each tile (🔓) public sealed class FloorIdGridSection : LotArchitectureSection Inheritance object LotArchitectureSection FloorIdGridSection Inherited Members LotArchitectureSection.Type object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The grid has SizeX × SizeZ tiles per layer and four ids per tile, one per FloorQuarter. Each id is a Id of the lot's FloorKeysSection, whose key is a CTProductFloorPattern (0xB4F762C9); 0 means no floor. The types Floors, Ceilings, PoolSurfaces, SecondaryFloors and CeilingPaints have one layer per level of the lot (HasLevels), indexed by level − LowestLevel, so ground level is index −LowestLevel. TerrainFloors and PondBottoms have a single layer, for ground level. When the lot's Version is 8 or less, PoolSurfaces also has a single layer, for ground level. Roles proven by the game's code and in-game tests: Floors is the floor pattern of each level, TerrainFloors the floor pattern painted on bare terrain, PondBottoms the pond bottom pattern and CeilingPaints the ceiling paint. In-game tests show that building a room fills Ceilings at the level above the room over exactly the room's tiles (and painting the ceiling changes only CeilingPaints), and that building a pool fills PoolSurfaces over exactly the pool's tiles at the level above the pool's block; the game's code assigns both grids to the room on the level below their layer. In-game tests show that building a room or a platform fills SecondaryFloors over its tiles with the lot's default floor key, and that painting a floor or a platform's top changes only Floors; the role of SecondaryFloors, which covers the same quarters as Floors, is still unknown. The layers are stored one after another, each as SizeX rows of SizeZ tiles of four little-endian 16-bit ids; the section has no version. architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Flo.title: Class FloorRotationGridSection | Llama Logic
architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Flo.summary: Class FloorRotationGridSection Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Represents one of the five floor rotation grids: the rotation of the pattern on each quarter of each tile of a FloorIdGridSection (🔓) public sealed class FloorRotationGridSection : LotArchitectureSection Inheritance object LotArchitectureSection FloorRotationGridSection Inherited Members LotArchitectureSection.Type object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The grid has SizeX × SizeZ tiles per layer and one rotation of 0 through 3 per FloorQuarter. A rotation is the number of 90° clockwise turns of the pattern, as seen in game: rotating one floor tile by 90° changed all four of its quarters from 0 to 1, and so did turning a terrain floor tile 90° clockwise (in-game tests). Each grid is paired with a floor id grid: FloorRotations with Floors, CeilingRotations with Ceilings, SecondaryFloorRotations with SecondaryFloors, CeilingPaintRotations with CeilingPaints and TerrainFloorRotations with TerrainFloors; FloorIdGridSection describes the roles of the id grids and the in-game tests and code that show them. All types but TerrainFloorRotations have one layer per level of the lot (HasLevels), indexed by level − LowestLevel; TerrainFloorRotations has a single layer, for ground level. The layers are stored one after another, each as SizeX rows of SizeZ bytes; each byte holds the four rotations of a tile, two bits each, the NegativeZ quarter in the lowest bits, as the game's getter and setter read and write them. The section has no version. architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Lot.summary: Class LotArchitecture Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Represents the architecture of a lot: its walls, floors, roofs, stairs, terrain and the rest of its build, as typed sections (🔓) public sealed class LotArchitecture Inheritance object LotArchitecture Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The game stores a lot's architecture as a RecordBundle in three places: the WorldLotArchitecture resources of world files, the architecture data of each lot in a save game (see ZoneArchitecture) and tray blueprints (see Blueprint). Each record of the bundle is one section, keyed by its LotArchitectureSectionType, group 0 and instance 1. Many sections can only be read with the lot's dimensions, which the LotSize section gives, so the bundle, not the section, is the unit of decoding. Records Decode(RecordBundle) cannot turn into sections are kept, unchanged, in UndecodedRecords: those of types this library does not know, those with another group or instance, those with a version (of the section or of an element of it) or a floor feature layer type this library does not support, and those that need dimensions an older LotSize section does not give (the game itself discards those). Encode() writes the sections in the layout of their versions, so decoding and encoding the architecture of any lot the game wrote reproduces it byte for byte. Where the documentation of the sections speaks of the lots, sections or entries examined, it means the 2,919 lot architectures examined while developing this library, at the game's patch level as of October 2026: those of the lots of the game's installed world files (of which twelve base-game worlds had been replaced by a community lot-replacement mod), the 179 lots of the Maxis originals of those twelve worlds, the lots of four save games and 73 tray blueprints. architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Lot.summary: Class LotInfoSection Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Represents the LotInfo section: the lot's levels, style, blueprint and users (🔓) public sealed class LotInfoSection : LotArchitectureSection Inheritance object LotArchitectureSection LotInfoSection Inherited Members LotArchitectureSection.Type object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The layout is Unknown1 (from version 13 on), the lowest and highest levels (signed bytes), one height per level from the lowest to the highest, LevelElevationOffset (from version 6 on), NegativeLevelElevationOffset (from version 16 on), Unknown2 (from version 17 on), Unknown3 (from version 18 on) and StyleKey (from version 7 on). From version 11 on, BlueprintInstance, the ids of the two users, Uuid, the names of the two users and, from version 19 on, the rest of the two user records follow. Versions 12 through 14 end with one plex map entry (value and has-value flag) and versions 15 and later with a 32-bit entry count and the entries. The highest level is not kept: it is LowestLevel plus the number of LevelHeights minus 1, which the game's reader relies on to read the heights. The number of heights equals LevelCount. Versions 5 through 20 are supported, and the game writes version 20. The game reads some other sections only for some versions of this one (for example PendingPlacementSection from version 9 on). It is signed, −1 through 1, and defaults to 0. Direction Gets/sets the direction of the roof, a value of the game's eight-way direction enumeration public byte Direction { get; set; } Property Value byte Remarks The game rotates it in steps of the eight-way enumeration (modulo 8); it is 0, 2, 4 or 6 in every lot examined. The game writes 3 and its reader reads any value, laying out the roof as for 3 when the value is 3 or more; this library supports 0 through 3. architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Wal.title: Class WallBlock | Llama Logic
architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Wal.summary: Class WallBlock Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Represents a block: a room, platform, wall line, fence line, pool or fountain, as loops of segments on one level, with the catalog products along them public sealed class WallBlock Inheritance object WallBlock Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks This is the game's WallInfo, which WallBlocksSection and PlexesSection both store; the layout follows the game's reader and writer. Versions 17 through 36 are supported, and the game writes version 36. The game reads versions 18 through 36; in the lots examined, version 17 appears only where the LotSizeSection is version 2, and its layout is the game's layout for version 18 plus Unknown1. The lots examined hold versions 17, 22, 29, 31, 32, 33, 35 and 36; the layouts of the other versions follow the game's reader. Layout, with version gates: Version (ushort), Id, Level, Unknown1 (17), BlockType (after 24), PlexId (after 35), HasFloor, Unknown3 (after 27), BaseElevation, FloorHeightOffset (after 33), Unknown4 (31 and 32), then before 27: Unknown5, Unknown6 (before 22), LegacyKeys (type, group, instance), Unknown7, Unknown8; then a ushort loop count (after 23; one loop before), the Loops, Unknown9 (before 19), Products (after 19), LegacyStamp (12 through 25), and before 27 Unknown10, Unknown11 and Unknown12. Each segment stores these product slots: none before version 20 (the game takes all from LegacyKeys), slots 0 through 3 in versions 20 through 26 (the game takes slots 4 through 8 from LegacyKeys), 0 through 6 in versions 27 and 28, 0 through 7 in versions 29 and 32 through 34, and all nine in versions 30, 31, 35 and 36. Properties BaseElevation Gets/sets the elevation of the block's base, in meters public float BaseElevation { get; set; } Property Value float Remarks The game sets it to the elevation of Level plus the lot's offset; adding a foundation raised it by 0.25 (in-game test). It is −0.375 or −0.125 for fountains in the lots examined, and it was −3 for a new pool (in-game test). BlockType Gets/sets the type of the block public WallBlockType BlockType { get; set; } Property Value WallBlockType Remarks Stored from version 25 on; the game treats older blocks as Standard. FloorHeightOffset Gets/sets the offset of the floor from BaseElevation, in meters public float FloorHeightOffset { get; set; } Property Value float Remarks The game checks it with FloorHeightOffsetOutOfBounds before setting it and takes the block's bottom as the lower of BaseElevation and BaseElevation plus this offset. Raising a room's floor one step changed it from 0 to 0.25, and a platform had 0.25 when drawn and 0.5 after one raise (in-game tests); the game stores a platform as a block like a room, so a raised room floor and a platform differ in the data only by their segments, which are Open where a platform has no walls. Stored from version 34 on. HasFloor Gets/sets whether the block has a floor public bool HasFloor { get; set; } Property Value bool Remarks Deleting the entire floor of a room changed only this value of the room's block, from true to false (in-game test). The game keeps it at offset 0x80 of the block, sets it to whether the level is at most 0 when it copies blocks into a plex and needs it for FloorHeightOffset. In the lots examined it is 1 for every pool and fountain block, for 36,076 of the 51,425 Standard blocks and for 5,271 of the 11,629 Fence blocks. Id Gets/sets the id of the block public ushort Id { get; set; } Property Value ushort Remarks The game keys its blocks by this id and drops a block whose id is 0. The game renumbers the blocks when it saves: the same rooms had different ids from one save to the next (in-game test). LegacyKeys Gets the catalog keys that versions before 27 store for the whole block public Collection<ResourceKey> LegacyKeys { get; } Property Value Collection<ResourceKey> Remarks Versions before 21 store 15 keys, versions 21 through 26 store 9. Of 15, the game uses positions 1, 2 and 5 for slots 0, 1 and 2, positions 3 and 4 for slot 7 (the later one wins), position 8 for slot 3 and positions 12 through 14 for slots 4 through 6; of 9, it uses positions 6 through 8 for slots 4 through 6. It reads the other positions as four uint values and discards them; in the lots examined they hold floor, window set and object catalog keys or the null key. LegacyStamp Gets/sets the value versions 12 through 25 store once for the whole block in place of each segment's FenceStamp and CeilingRailStamp public uint LegacyStamp { get; set; } Property Value uint Remarks The game copies it into both values of every segment. Level Gets/sets the lot level of the block public sbyte Level { get; set; } Property Value sbyte Remarks The game restricts the level by BlockType and takes the block's level height from it. Loops Gets the loops of the block public Collection<WallBlockLoop> Loops { get; } Property Value Collection<WallBlockLoop> Remarks Versions before 24 hold exactly one loop. 1 through 12 in the lots examined. PlexId Gets/sets the id of the plex (unit) the block belongs to public ushort PlexId { get; set; } Property Value ushort Remarks The game's plex manager sets it; 300 is the shared plex. The values match the ids of the PlexesSection plexes. Stored from version 36 on. Products Gets the table of the catalog products the segments refer to public ProductTable Products { get; } Property Value ProductTable Remarks Stored from version 20 on. Unknown1 Gets/sets a byte version 17 stores after Level public byte Unknown1 { get; set; } Property Value byte Remarks It equals Level in every lot examined. The game's reader has no such byte. Unknown10 Gets/sets a ushort versions before 27 store at the end of the block public ushort Unknown10 { get; set; } Property Value ushort Remarks The game reads it and discards it. 4 in every lot examined. Unknown11 Gets/sets a byte versions before 27 store after Unknown10 public byte Unknown11 { get; set; } Property Value byte Remarks The game reads it and discards it. 1 in every lot examined. Unknown12 Gets/sets a byte versions before 27 store after Unknown11 public byte Unknown12 { get; set; } Property Value byte Remarks The game reads it and discards it. 1 in every lot examined. Unknown3 Gets/sets a Boolean the game keeps at offset 0x81 of the block public bool Unknown3 { get; set; } Property Value bool Remarks Hypothesis: whether the block has an automatic ceiling. The game sets it to whether every outer segment has a wall or the level is below 0, and clears it when it copies blocks into a plex. In the lots examined it is 0 for every Fence block, 1 for every fountain block, 1 for 466 of the 482 pool blocks and for 22,161 of the 51,182 Standard blocks that store it. In in-game tests a new fence block and a platform had 0 and enclosed rooms had 1, which is consistent with the hypothesis. Stored from version 28 on. The game reads them as nine slots; which slots a block version stores is described with Version, and the game fills the slots an older version does not store from the block's LegacyKeys. The slot names follow the catalog types the slots refer to in every lot examined (names from the game's CTProduct table). Layout: the loop stores X and Z of all its segments first, then, per segment, Kind, Unknown1 (versions before 23), the stored slots in slot order, then FenceStamp and CeilingRailStamp (versions after 25). Adding a foundation set it, together with FenceStamp, to the value StampCounter was raised to (in-game test); what the game uses it for is unknown. Adding a foundation set it, together with CeilingRailStamp, to the value StampCounter was raised to (in-game test); what the game uses it for is unknown. Never 0 in the lots examined. architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Wal.title: Enum WallBlockSegmentKind | Llama Logic
architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Wal.summary: Enum WallBlockSegmentKind Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Specifies the kind of a WallBlockSegment [SuppressMessage("Design", "CA1028: Enum Storage should be Int32", Justification = "The game stores the value as a byte.")] public enum WallBlockSegmentKind : byte Fields ModularPiece = 2 A segment of a modular piece without a wall ModularPieceWithWall = 3 A segment of a modular piece with a wall Open = 1 A segment without a wall Wall = 0 A segment with a wall Remarks The game treats a block as enclosed when none of the segments of its outer loop is Open or ModularPiece, emits CantPlacePoolUnderWall for a Wall segment, and requires ModularPiece or ModularPieceWithWall on a diagonal segment flanked by 45° segments of the same kind, otherwise InvalidBlockModularPieceConfiguration. That such segments form rounded corners is a hypothesis. Before block version 27 the game maps the stored values 0 through 3 to 0, 1, 2 and 1 with a table.

architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Wal.title: Enum WallBlockType | Llama Logic
architecture/LlamaLogic.Architecture.Wal.summary: Enum WallBlockType Namespace LlamaLogic.Architecture Assembly LlamaLogic.Architecture.dll Specifies the type of a WallBlock [SuppressMessage("Design", "CA1028: Enum Storage should be Int32", Justification = "The game stores the value as a byte.")] public enum WallBlockType : byte Fields Fence = 1 A fence line Placing a fence creates a block of this type (in-game test). The game allows it only at level 0 and gives it no elevation. Fountain = 2 A fountain The game emits CantPlaceFountainUnderAnything for it, gives it a height of 0.375 and allows it only at level -1. Pool = 3 A pool The game emits CantPlacePoolUnderOtherPool for it; placing a pool creates a block of this type (in-game test). Standard = 0 A block that is not a fence, fountain or pool In the lots examined these are rooms and free-standing wall lines, and a platform is a block of this type too: drawing one creates a block whose segments are all Open until walls are added, raised by FloorHeightOffset just as a room whose floor is raised (in-game tests); that the type covers nothing else is a hypothesis. Remarks The game checks each block type against the WallBlockSegmentKind of the block's segments with a table: a Fence block allows only Open, a Fountain or Pool block only Wall and ModularPieceWithWall (otherwise BlockTypeIncompatibleWithProduct).

packages/LlamaLogic.Packages.Compression.title: Enum CompressionMode | Llama Logic
packages/LlamaLogic.Packages.Compression.summary: Enum CompressionMode Namespace LlamaLogic.Packages Assembly LlamaLogic.Packages.dll Represents the compression mode to use when setting the content of a resource in a DataBasePackedFile public enum CompressionMode Fields Auto = 0 The library will choose whether and how to compress the data or not CallerSuppliedInternal = 6 ⚠️ The data will not be processed for compression by the library and the resource will be marked as having been compressed using Maxis' internal method; accepted by SetRaw(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, int) and SetRawAsync(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, int, CancellationToken) only, which also take the decompressed size (use with caution) CallerSuppliedStreamable = 7 ⚠️ The data will not be processed for compression by the library and the resource will be marked as having been compressed using Maxis' streamable method; accepted by SetRaw(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, int) and SetRawAsync(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, int, CancellationToken) only, which also take the decompressed size (use with caution) CallerSuppliedZLib = 8 ⚠️ The data will not be processed for compression by the library and the resource will be marked as having been compressed using ZLIB; accepted by SetRaw(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, int) and SetRawAsync(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, int, CancellationToken) only, which also take the decompressed size (use with caution) ForceInternal = 4 The data will be compressed using Maxis' internal method ForceOff = 1 The data will not be compressed [Obsolete("This setting can no longer be used and will be removed in a future version. If you need to force a compression, use a different force member of this enum.", true)] ForceOn = 2 Deprecated: do not use ForceZLib = 3 The data will be compressed using ZLib SetDeletedFlag = 5 ⚠️ The data will not be processed for compression by the library—thus callers will need to invoke ZLibCompress(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>) or ZLibCompressAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) themselves and pass the result to Set(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode) or SetAsync(ResourceKey, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CompressionMode, CancellationToken), respectively, if they intend for the content to be compressed with ZLib despite being flagged—and the deleted flag will be set (use with caution) Remarks Important: While this library does support the older compression methods, it does not have a complete catalog of how to do so properly for every resource type automatically (Auto). If you want to be sure that you're compressing a resource correctly, utilize GetExplicitCompressionMode(ResourceKey) with a package the game is currently accepting. Warning: The Sims 4 does not always expect or tolerate ZLib compression for certain types of resources, such as for world package files which ship with the game (see thepancake1's comment about this on the Creator Musings Discord for more information).

packages/LlamaLogic.Packages.DataBasePac.summary: Class DataBasePackedFile Namespace LlamaLogic.Packages Assembly LlamaLogic.Packages.dll Represents a Maxis DBPF format package file (🔒) public sealed class DataBasePackedFile : IAsyncDisposable, IDisposable Inheritance object DataBasePackedFile Implements IAsyncDisposable IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Streams and Disposal When a package is opened by this class from a Stream, the class assumes ownership of the Stream. Manipulating the Stream afterward may result in undefined behavior. The class will dispose of the Stream when it is, itself, disposed. To use the Save(bool, ResourceKeyOrder) or SaveAsync(bool, ResourceKeyOrder, CancellationToken) methods, the package must have been opened from a Stream which is writeable. This can also be determined by the caller in advance of attempting to use them by checking the value of the CanSaveInPlace property. However, for ease of use in web frameworks like ASP.NET Core, the CopyTo(Stream, ResourceKeyOrder) and CopyToAsync(Stream, ResourceKeyOrder, CancellationToken) methods do not require that the Stream which they are passed is seekable. Lazy Loading When a package is first opened using this class, the package index is read but the content of the package resources is not. All of the retrieval methods of this class have async counterparts for callers who prefer not to be blocked by I/O operations which may be required when retrieving resource content. Because resource names (when applicable) are determined by their content, this class will not index resource names until they are first referenced, either explicitly by calling GetNames() or GetNamesAsync(CancellationToken), or implicitly by calling any of the other methods which deal with resource names. Afterward, the names are cached for the lifetime of the package instance and updated as the caller sets the content of resources or deletes them. Thread Safety All properties and methods of this class, including async methods, are kept thread-safe with internally managed locks. Async methods which accept cancellation tokens will honor signals so long as they have not progressed to mutating the state of the package. Compression Decompression of resource content is handled automatically by this class. When retrieving resource content, this class will automatically decompress it using either proprietary Maxis internal or streaming compression, or ZLib compression. When saving resources, this class will always use ZLib compression. For more details, see the remarks for the CompressionMode enumeration. Resource content is compressed in memory when it is set to minimize the amount of memory used while operating on a package. Deleted Entries This class honors the deleted entry flag in the package index under normal circumstances. If a caller attempts to retrieve the content of a resource flagged as deleted, the class will throw a FileNotFoundException by default. All retrieval methods have an optional force bool parameter which, when true, will cause the class to attempt to retrieve the content of a resource flagged as deleted (this is not guaranteed to work). While it will permit the caller to specify any version they like, it does not guard against potential negative consequences which may result from such packages actually being used. The default version for newly created packages is currently 2.1. Versions 1.x (used by The Sims 2) are written with the 1.x header and index layouts, compress only with Maxis' internal algorithm, and record which resources are compressed in a directory resource (type, group, and instance E86B1EEF, E86B1EEF, 286B1F03) which this class brings up to date whenever it writes the package, removing it when no resources are compressed. unlike vgmstream, it lays the audio out at a constant bitrate with a bit reservoir and adds a gapless playback tag, so that ordinary MP3 decoders play it sample for sample as the game does Methods CreateFromMp3(ElectronicArtsAudioCoreMp3) Makes a sound for The Sims 4 from the MP3s GetMp3(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>) rebuilt from one, without re-encoding them, stored as the original was public static ElectronicArtsAudioCoreSound CreateFromMp3(ElectronicArtsAudioCoreMp3 mp3) Parameters mp3 ElectronicArtsAudioCoreMp3 Returns ElectronicArtsAudioCoreSound Exceptions InvalidDataException An MP3 is malformed NotSupportedException The sound is not one this can make CreateFromMp3(IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyList<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>>, ElectronicArtsAudioCoreStorage, bool) Makes a sound for The Sims 4 from MP3s, without re-encoding them public static ElectronicArtsAudioCoreSound CreateFromMp3(IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyList<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>> segments, ElectronicArtsAudioCoreStorage storage, bool isLooping) Parameters segments IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyList<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>> The MP3s of the sound: one segment, or, for a sound that loops from somewhere other than its start, the part before the loop and the loop; each segment's MP3s are layers played together (all stereo, except that the last may be mono), with the same number of frames storage ElectronicArtsAudioCoreStorage Where the game should find the audio isLooping bool Whether the sound loops (from its start, with one segment; from the start of the second segment, with two) Returns ElectronicArtsAudioCoreSound Exceptions ArgumentException segments is empty, has more than two segments, has two without isLooping, or has a segment without MP3s InvalidDataException An MP3 is malformed, the MP3s disagree about their sample rate, layout or length, or the sound is too long for storage NotSupportedException An MP3 is not MPEG-1 Layer III (32,000, 44,100 or 48,000 Hz), or storage is Gigasample CreateFromMp3(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, ElectronicArtsAudioCoreStorage, bool) Makes a sound for The Sims 4 from an MP3, without re-encoding it public static ElectronicArtsAudioCoreSound CreateFromMp3(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> mp3Data, ElectronicArtsAudioCoreStorage storage, bool isLooping = false) Parameters mp3Data ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The MP3: MPEG-1 Layer III (32,000, 44,100 or 48,000 Hz), mono or stereo, constant or variable bitrate (not free format) storage ElectronicArtsAudioCoreStorage Where the game should find the audio: Memory (in the AudioVocals resource) or Stream (in an AudioEffects resource with the same instance) isLooping bool Whether the sound loops from its start Returns ElectronicArtsAudioCoreSound Remarks The sound's length comes from the MP3's gapless playback tag (as LAME and the tools built on it write); an MP3 without one is taken to end where its last frame does. packages/LlamaLogic.Packages.Models.ModF.summary: Class ModFileManifestModel Namespace LlamaLogic.Packages.Models.ModFileManifest Assembly LlamaLogic.Packages.dll Represents a mod file manifest SnippetTuning resource (🔓) public sealed class ModFileManifestModel : Model, IModel<ModFileManifestModel>, IModel, IXmlSerializable Inheritance object Model ModFileManifestModel Implements IModel<ModFileManifestModel> IModel IXmlSerializable Inherited Members Model.Decode(ResourceType, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>) Model.GetModelType(ResourceType) Model.GetName(ResourceType, Stream) Model.GetNameAsync(ResourceType, Stream, CancellationToken) object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks This model allows callers to easily create, read, and update a mod file manifest. These manifests are a format sponsored by the Llama Logic team to permit creators to specify the dependency requirements of their mods. Use in Mod Package (.package) files When originally creating packages, place one and only one mod file manifest SnippetTuning resource in the package and use sufficiently unique values for its FullInstance and TuningName. If an external application encounters multiple SnippetTuning manifest resources in a package, it must assume that a manifest un-aware tool has merged multiple manifested packages and process each manifest accordingly. Avoid using Group 0x00000000 as this is informally reserved for Maxis. It would be a bizarre miracle if they started incorporating dependency information using a community format. Regardless, let's not make them feel unwelcome and hold their spot for them. Use in Script Mod Archive (.ts4script) files Because these files are just ZIP archives with a different extension and their contents are not flatly merged by the game as the contents of package files are, there is no risk of collision. Also, since they need not contend with game resource management, they need not be in an arcane format like XML, so they are in YAML instead. The static parsing methods of this type expect YAML representations of manifests and the ToString() method produces them. Name your mod file manifest resource llamalogic.modfilemanifest.yml and put it in the root of your .ts4script archive. packages/LlamaLogic.Packages.Models.SimD.summary: Enum SimDataType Namespace LlamaLogic.Packages.Models.SimData Assembly LlamaLogic.Packages.dll A type of data within a SimData resource public enum SimDataType Fields BOOL = 0 A bool expressed with an entire byte (0 is false, any other value is true) CHAR8 = 1 A single byte of a UTF-8 string FLOAT = 10 A float FLOAT2 = 15 You might think it's a double, but nope: two floats FLOAT3 = 16 An obvious trend is developing, for this is three floats FLOAT4 = 17 (You know when, every once in a while, there's a great trilogy and someone messes it up?) Here are your four floats HASHEDSTRING8 = 12 An int offset to a null-terminated UTF-8 string and its accompanying Fnv32 hash INT16 = 4 A short INT32 = 6 An int INT64 = 8 A long INT8 = 2 An sbyte LOCKEY = 20 A four-byte key used to uniquely identify localized strings in The Sims 4 (typically the Fnv32 hash of the string in its original language) OBJECT = 13 An int offset to an object RESOURCEKEY = 19 A ResourceKey laid out by FullInstance, then Type, then Group STRING8 = 11 An int offset to a null-terminated UTF-8 string TABLESETREFERENCE = 18 It's not just about good manners from "How to Serve and Not Be Served", it's really about this ulong Seriously, though, why have these when we already have UINT64, you ask? you’re right that table set refs are just uint64s, but it is important to distinguish them because they mean different things. int64s are just literal numbers, table set refs are tuning IDs. so, when the game loads these, it knows that uint64 is just a number, so leave it alone, whereas a table set ref is tuning, so it needs to look that tuning up and use it as the value there rather than the number itself — frankk, August 16, 2024 in Lot 51's Discord UINT16 = 5 A ushort UINT32 = 7 A uint UINT64 = 9 A ulong UINT8 = 3 A byte VARIANT = 21 An int offset to an object accompanied by a uint type hash VECTOR = 14 An int offset to an array of objects and a uint that is its size

Decode(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>) supports the chunks the game's world files contain and rejects the others the game can also read (MODL, DEFG, LEVL, SCRP, TRES, REFS, SIZY), whose layouts are not established. tuning-descriptions/LlamaLogic.TuningDes.title: Class SimDataGenerator | Llama Logic
tuning-descriptions/LlamaLogic.TuningDes.summary: Class SimDataGenerator Namespace LlamaLogic.TuningDescriptions Assembly LlamaLogic.TuningDescriptions.dll Generates SimData resources from tuning the way Maxis' build does, using the tuning descriptions of the game version for which they are generated (🔒) public sealed class SimDataGenerator Inheritance object SimDataGenerator Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Which tunables become columns, the columns' types, and the values written for tuning that omits a tunable all come from Descriptions. Some of what Maxis' build knows is not in tuning descriptions, so the generator learns it: AddTuning(XDocument) and AddTuning(CombinedTuningModel) learn the entries of dynamic enumerations (such as tags defined by module tuning) and the instances of tuning that is referenced by name AddLayouts(SimDataModel) learns the column order of schemas the game reads with a layout of its own (such as Client_* and Renderer.* schemas), whose columns are otherwise ordered by name Maxis' build also converts some resource keys: a PNGImage key in tuning is written to SimData as a DSTImage key, and an AudioConfigurationReference key as an AudioConfiguration key in group 0x001407EC. The generator does the same unless RemoveResourceKeyConversion(ResourceType, uint) says otherwise, and AddResourceKeyConversion(ResourceType, uint, ResourceType, uint) adds conversions. For the game's own SimData, the game's combined tuning and SimData are the sources of what the generator needs to learn. Constructors SimDataGenerator(TuningDescriptionSet) Initializes a new SimDataGenerator public SimDataGenerator(TuningDescriptionSet descriptions) Parameters descriptions TuningDescriptionSet The tuning descriptions of the game version for which SimData will be generated Properties Descriptions Gets the tuning descriptions of the game version for which SimData is generated public TuningDescriptionSet Descriptions { get; } Property Value TuningDescriptionSet Methods AddLayouts(SimDataModel) Learns the column order of each schema in the specified simData whose columns are not ordered by name public void AddLayouts(SimDataModel simData) Parameters simData SimDataModel Remarks When generating an object of a schema with the same name and the same columns, the generator orders the columns as they are ordered in simData. AddResourceKeyConversion(ResourceType, uint, ResourceType, uint) Learns that resource keys of the specified fromType and fromGroup in tuning are written to SimData with the specified toType and toGroup public void AddResourceKeyConversion(ResourceType fromType, uint fromGroup, ResourceType toType, uint toGroup) Parameters fromType ResourceType fromGroup uint toType ResourceType toGroup uint AddTuning(CombinedTuningModel) Learns the entries of dynamic enumerations and the names of instances from each tuning in the specified combinedTuning public void AddTuning(CombinedTuningModel combinedTuning) Parameters combinedTuning CombinedTuningModel AddTuning(XDocument) Learns the entries of dynamic enumerations the specified tuning defines (if it is module tuning) and the name of its instance public void AddTuning(XDocument tuning) Parameters tuning XDocument Remarks An instance or enumeration value that is not a decimal number (such as one a modding tool wrote in hexadecimal) is not learned. Generate(XDocument) Generates the SimData for the specified tuning public SimDataModel Generate(XDocument tuning) Parameters tuning XDocument Instance tuning (an I element) or module tuning (an M element) Returns SimDataModel The SimData, with one instance for instance tuning or one instance for each class of module tuning that has exported tunables Remarks The Pack of the SimData is 0, the base game's; set it for SimData that belongs to a pack. Exceptions SimDataGenerationException tuning cannot be generated with Descriptions and what the generator has learned RemoveResourceKeyConversion(ResourceType, uint) Stops converting resource keys of the specified fromType and fromGroup in tuning, so that they are written to SimData as they are public void RemoveResourceKeyConversion(ResourceType fromType, uint fromGroup) Parameters fromType ResourceType fromGroup uint

tuning-descriptions/LlamaLogic.TuningDes.summary: Class TuningDescriptionSet Namespace LlamaLogic.TuningDescriptions Assembly LlamaLogic.TuningDescriptions.dll Represents a set of tuning descriptions for a version of The Sims 4, as Maxis distributes it (🔒) public sealed class TuningDescriptionSet : IDisposable Inheritance object TuningDescriptionSet Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A set is indexed by the paths of its documents when it is opened: instances are */Descriptions/{class}.tdesc, modules are Tuning/{module with . replaced by -}.tdesc, and fragments are TdescFrag/{class}.tdescfrag. A document is read the first time it is requested, and it may be read again once nothing refers to it any longer, so requesting a document twice does not necessarily return the same object. A set's members are safe to use from multiple threads.
